tasks.title: Ledger format 4 preserves history and commits alert state with pending deliveries
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, ledger responsibility; R9 in full at the storage boundary; R1 atomic pending-incident drop mutation; R7 delivery-retention compatibility; Counterexamples / Transaction failure and crash recovery (storage guarantees), Alert-state pruning, Ledger format and Migration crash with committed WAL data; completion checks 5 and 6. Implement validated format-4 alert_state rows and their mirror. Follow R9's migration sequence exactly: validate format 3 read-only without changing refused main/WAL/SHM bytes; checkpoint the validated source with synchronous FULL and wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE); require busy 0, log equal to checkpointed, and WAL absent or empty after close, otherwise throw ledger checkpoint was blocked without deleting source files, writing a backup or leaving .migrating; re-read and validate read-only; unlink the old .v3.bak without following symlinks and byte-copy the checkpointed main file using pinned kit writeFileAtomicSync with mode 0600; publish through the private wx .migrating path and fsync. Add afterSidecars between sidecar removal and rename, alongside beforePublish. Preserve every channel, mark, entry, payload and recipient record; log migration from 3; JSON 1/2 migrate directly to 4. Test every migration crash-table row using three entries only in committed WAL frames, independently verifying 0 rows in the pre-checkpoint main file and 3 in the checkpointed source/backup and recovered format 4. Include repeated interrupted opens, a blocked checkpoint, and hostile rows only in WAL. Expose one batch mutation for all alert-row changes including observed_at-only advances and missing per-channel pending entries, with memory updated only after commit and no write for an empty batch. Add a separate mutation that drops all pending incident/payloadless entries across all given warning-only channels in one transaction, clears payloads/recipients, preserves pending warnings and failed records, returns per-channel counts, and writes nothing when there is nothing to drop. T3 wires it into construction and handles startup failure. Add feed-presence-aware alert-state pruning support independent of delivery retention; no good feed visibility means no pruning. Use existing incident payloads for storage tests now; T2 adds warning-payload round trips. Update the exact schema/version assertions permitted by the spec and add user_version 5 refusal; keep both hostile format-3-schema/user_version-4 fixtures unchanged. In test/reminders.test.ts:149, change only assert.equal(state.version, 3) to assert.equal(state.version, 4), since savedState reads PRAGMA user_version; preserve the key list on lines 145-148 and all other reminder expectations. This assertion update ships in T1 with the format bump, so the existing full suite remains green at this task boundary. Document migration, private files, pruning and downgrade. In docs/troubleshooting.md, change the cannot use state file row from user_version other than 3 to other than 3 or 4, and explain that a valid format-3 file is migrated rather than refused (R11). Keep lint, typecheck and the existing full suite green. Before feature work, capture the config rejection red baseline below in a writable origin/main scratch checkout and retain it for T3; never edit read-only context clones.

acceptance.expected: Run in the origin/main scratch checkout: nonzero exit with config: unknown key "alerts" in channels[0]. Retain this failing acceptance baseline; parseConfig does not create the output file.

acceptance.command: bun test test/ledger.v4.test.ts test/ledger.test.ts test/ledger.v2.test.ts test/prune.test.ts test/security-ledger-permissions.test.ts test/index.test.ts test/reminders.test.ts
acceptance.expected: 0 fail in this focused run (coverage exit status is not the gate). A valid format-3 fixture opens with user_version 4, backup user_version 3 and mode 0600, all previous records equal to the fixture, and no migration on a second open. Invalid format 3, format 4 without alert_state, user_version 5, stage 7 and kind x are refused with source bytes unchanged. Backup symlinks become regular files with mode 0600 while target bytes and mode stay unchanged. beforeCommit failure leaves 0 added alert rows and 0 added pending entries in memory and after reopen; successful batches and observed_at-only advances survive reopen. Atomic incident drop over two warning-only channels rolls back every entry on failure, and on success leaves 0 targeted pending incident entries, unchanged pending warnings and failed records, cleared dropped payloads/recipients and literal per-channel counts. Every alert-state pruning table row has its specified kept/removed result. The existing older reminder keys are pruned from the ledger test passes with saved state version exactly 4 and keys exactly ["1:opened","1:reminder:2"]; only its version literal changes from 3 to 4.

acceptance.command: bun test test/ledger.v4.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'committed WAL survives sidecar crash'
acceptance.expected: 0 fail on the candidate for the named regression covering the full Migration crash with committed WAL data table: the fixture main alone starts with 0 entries; after afterSidecars throws, source and backup each independently show user_version 3 and exactly 3 entries; a clean reopen shows version 4 and exactly 3 entries with delivered, failed and pending statuses, and the backup still has 3. Repeating the interrupted open twice preserves 3 backup entries. beforePublish interruption also recovers 3. A blocked checkpoint throws ledger checkpoint was blocked, retains 3 committed source/WAL entries and leaves no backup or .migrating; a hostile WAL row is refused with source and WAL bytes unchanged. In a writable candidate scratch copy with only the checkpoint step omitted, the crash/reopen regression fails with actual 0 entries versus literal expected 3; retain that failure line for the PR. Focused coverage is not the gate.

exit 0 for lint, typecheck and the full suite with at least 80% line coverage and cognitive complexity at most 15. The existing reminder suite passes with only test/reminders.test.ts:149's format literal changed from 3 to 4 and its key-list assertion unchanged. Both hostile format-3-schema/user_version-4 fixtures remain refused without expectation changes; the new user_version-5 refusal passes. Shared tooling, CI and dependency pins are unchanged.

tasks.title: Warning rules produce stable events that every sender can deliver and resend
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, types, pure budget/expiry modules, routing and sender responsibilities; R5-R8 and R10; R9 warning-payload round trips and failed CLI compatibility; Counterexamples / Budget, Expiry, Restart-safe ordering, Routing and config (routing only), and Statistics display examples; completion checks 2 (rule tests), 5 (warning payload persistence) and 6. After T1's config red baseline, write budget once-per-24-hour tests red first, then expiry [14,3] and restart-order tests, before implementing the pure functions. Keep each rule's observation selection, transition and key construction together, taking parsed contract types, nowMs and committed stored state and returning notifications plus proposed state changes. Cover every budget/expiry counterexample, separate check/component identity, strict thresholds and boundary times, no recovery reset or downtime burst, observation freshness/order, durable observed_at advances when stage is unchanged, type changes retaining the expiry row, and rearm only above 14 days. Persist proposed changes using T1's ledger in the complete restart-safe ordering table. Make Notification an event-discriminated union with unchanged incident fields/JSON and R8 warning shapes. Preserve the detector's incident-only NotificationEvent domain; make incident builder return types in notifier and incident fixture helpers precise where needed to keep this task type-correct, without changing incident behavior or assertions. Keep the reminder stale predicate narrowed on event, so warnings are never stale. Add optional channel subscription/control types; T3 owns parsing and operational use. Implement opt-in check/component routing, no member expansion, independent of sendIncidents. Support all five senders: raw webhook/file JSON, signed idempotency, cleaned and escaped names, warning labels, floor rounding, null availability, singular/zero-day text, status links, hideReason independence and email Message-ID. Prove warning pending/failed payloads survive reopen, T1's atomic drop preserves all three warning variants, and existing failed list/resend retains keys and shows all three events without changing failed-cli source. Narrow test/message and failed-cli incident helpers without changing expectations. Add fixtures and warning docs, including subscription/renewal limits; package description only, no dependency/pin changes. Leave lint, typecheck and the existing full suite green. T3 owns HTTP evaluation and meaningful origin/main failures of the same behavior tests; missing-module import failures do not count as red evidence.

acceptance.expected: 0 fail in this focused run. At threshold 25: budget 25 produces 0 events and 24.999 produces 1; after an event, +86399999 ms produces 0 more and +86400000 ms produces exactly 1. A check and component sharing id a produce 2 different keys. The expiry sequence 15,14,14,13,4,3,3,2,0,-1 produces exactly [14,3] for both TLS and domain; first observation 2 produces [3]. The six-step restart-order table persists observed_at t0+120000, does not rearm at step 3, emits 0 events at step 4 and exactly 1 milestone-14 event at step 6. Every remaining Budget and Expiry counterexample uses the spec's literal outcome; invalid, stale, equal and reordered readings make no state changes.

acceptance.command: bun test test/message.test.ts test/routing.test.ts test/webhook.test.ts test/failed-cli.test.ts test/channels.test.ts test/ledger.v4.test.ts
acceptance.expected: 0 fail in this focused run. Only subscribed and routed subjects are delivered, exclusions win, and sendIncidents false does not block warning routing. Budget display values 24.96, -3.25 and 99.8816 print 24.9, -3.3 and 99.881 respectively; raw JSON retains the unrounded inputs. All three labels and five sender formats match R8, including no data, 1 day and less than 1 day. Hostile names cannot inject Slack mentions or Teams markup. Webhook idempotency-key equals body key and signing remains valid. Pending and failed warning payloads round-trip unchanged, failed list shows the three event names, and failed resend retains the original key. Existing incident assertions and serialized payloads are unchanged.

exit 0 for lint, typecheck and the full suite with at least 80% line coverage and cognitive complexity at most 15. Existing incident expectations remain unchanged except T1's permitted ledger-format assertions; no unsafe casts fake incident fields, and no runtime dependency or pin changes.

tasks.title: Polling sends subscribed warnings durably and all integration and rollout checks pass
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, channel schema/config/index, API feeds/metrics and notifier responsibilities; R1-R4, R9 poll orchestration/pruning and integration of R5-R10; R11; every remaining Counterexample and completion checks 1-10; Performance impact, Security impact and Rollout order. Parse alerts and sendIncidents for all five channel types with exact R1 fixed messages/cross-field rules and ignored duplicates. Read threshold with kit readInt (fallback 25, min 0, max 100), wire it at startup and preserve suppression across edits. Preserve existing Settings equality assertions, for example using a separate threshold reader in config.ts; only the spec's named expectation changes are allowed. Preserve fetchChecks' default public behavior for incident names while also collecting CheckWithState inputs that pass both validators, only with alerts subscribed. Add validated components through the capped, timed, wire-checked no-redirect client, read only for budget-low subscriptions; 404 is absent and never a good visibility read. Add zero-valued components metric labels. Read enabled feeds in parallel, isolate errors/readiness accounting and do no second validation, components request or evaluation without subscriptions. In the Notifier constructor before start, invoke T1's single transaction for all warning-only channels' pending incident/legacy entries; on failure throw a named error with text cannot drop pending incident notifications of channels with sendIncidents false, aborting startup with no send/poll/ops bind. In index main, close the ledger, release the lock and rethrow on construction failure; test reacquisition on the same state path in test/index.test.ts. Log successful drops once per channel with count greater than 0. Keep warnings pending/resendable and failed incident records unchanged; skip legacy rebuild and seed new automatic/manual incident keys instead of enqueueing. On failed per-poll seed log incident seed failed, the next poll retries and enqueue nothing; detection retries the next poll. Preserve existing first-poll, routing-change and manual seeding. Successful incidents-off starts never replay old seeded/dropped keys after re-enable; a failed construction leaves the switch unapplied and old pending deliveries remain owed on a restart with sendIncidents true, exactly as the Failed drop, then re-enable table specifies. After per-channel incident/manual processing, gate each warning kind until all its subscribers have channel records; evaluate globally once, atomically commit all alert changes and routed pending payloads together, then enqueue. Persist every used expiry observation time, advance suppression even with no recipients, and retain last-good check/component visibility for hourly pruning with no pruning before a good read or on components 404. Keep warning events outside reminder stale handling. Add HTTP tests named budget once per 24 hours, expiry milestones 14 and 3, and expiry ordering survives restart through public entrypoints; run the same tests on writable origin/main scratch, copying only necessary fixtures, and retain meaningful assertion/startup failure lines, not missing-module errors. Cover every seeding/subscription, rollback/crash/pruning, sendIncidents and failed-drop table row, all config/feed failures, and unchanged incident JSON. Finish R11 docs and the full security checklist. Use writable scratch copies for main/deploy; do not edit context clones or committed deploy pins. Prepare temporary performance/fake-API harnesses outside the repository and set PULSE_571_DEPLOY_SCRATCH to writable deploy main with only notify's image replaced. The PR records checks 1-10, T1's checkpoint-omission regression failure, allowed expectation changes with each changed successful-open version assertion (including T1's test/reminders.test.ts:149 literal 3-to-4 update and unchanged reminder key list), unchanged hostile user_version-4 tests, added version-5 refusal, all security/performance/manual/Compose/CI evidence and known limits.

acceptance.command: bun test test/alerts.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'budget once per 24 hours|expiry milestones 14 and 3|expiry ordering survives restart'

acceptance.expected: 0 fail; every Counterexamples row has the literal expected result. HTTP fixture api-1 at budget 24 and TLS at 13 days sends exactly 1 budget-low and 1 tls-expiry per subscribed webhook channel, with equal body/header keys, and 0 warnings to the unsubscribed channel. Two HTTP 500 responses then 204 yield exactly 3 attempts with 1 key. Failed seeding of B yields 0 alerts and 0 alert rows for that kind until B seeds; then A and B receive the same key and B receives 0 old incidents. Late subscriptions and widened filters receive 0 replayed milestones. beforeCommit failure yields 0 alert rows, 0 pending entries and 0 receiver requests; the next good poll sends exactly 1 request per channel. A crash after commit resends the same pending key and generates 0 new keys.

0 fail (focused coverage is not the gate). A successful sendIncidents false restart drops the four stored incident keys and logs count 4, sends exactly 1 stored budget warning and 0 incidents across 10 polls. 9:opened is seeded; failed resend of 5:opened is dropped at next start; re-enable sends 0 old events and a later resolution sends exactly 1 key 9:resolved. Failed drop, then re-enable table: beforeCommit failure makes construction throw cannot drop pending incident notifications of channels with sendIncidents false, with 0 requests and exactly 2 still-pending entries (7:opened and the budget key). Restart with true sends exactly 2 requests, 7:opened once and that budget key once. Repeat from the initial fixture, fail construction, then successfully restart with false: exactly 1 request (budget), followed by 0 more over 10 polls after re-enabling true. A failing per-poll seed logs incident seed failed, the next poll retries, sends 0 requests and stores 9:opened as seeded on the next poll. On constructor failure main throws, closes the ledger and releases the lock; a second main on the same state path acquires it.

acceptance.command: bun test test/config.test.ts test/alerts.test.ts test/message.test.ts test/ledger.v4.test.ts test/security-ledger-permissions.test.ts test/metrics.test.ts
acceptance.expected: 0 fail; security fixtures reject hostile config, budget strings/non-finite JSON and fractional days with fixed messages; config errors never echo invalid values and API names/ids never enter logs. A 10000-character control/markup name is cleaned/escaped; colon/newline ids produce only a 32-hex hash suffix in keys. alerts absent or empty sends 0 warnings, duplicate subscriptions do not duplicate events; sendIncidents defaults true, while invalid types, false without nonempty alerts and false with reminders are refused with exact R1 text. Threshold 101, -1, 25.5, abc and 25abc fail startup; 0 and 100 start; at threshold 0 budget 0 sends 0 events and -0.1 sends 1. Second-validator failures preserve valid Check names and increment checks skipped metrics with fixed invalid/index logs. Oversized/302 components responses are refused; 404 leaves incidents and check budgets working; other feed failures affect readiness independently; no alerts means 0 components requests and 0 second-validator calls. New components metrics start at 0. Backup symlink target bytes/mode and refused main/WAL/SHM bytes are unchanged, private files have mode 0600, and stage 7/kind x are refused. Report every applicable Security impact checklist item.

Existing notifier, reminders, manual, routing-change, ledger, prune, webhook and channel suites pass with unchanged expectations except the format-4 schema/user_version assertion, components metric-label additions and direct successful-open user_version 3-to-4 assertions expressly allowed by the spec, each named in the PR, including test/reminders.test.ts:149's literal 3-to-4 update with the key list unchanged. The added user_version-5 case passes and both existing malformed user_version-4 fixtures still refuse open unchanged.

Run five times on origin/main and five times on the branch on the same machine; all ten full suites pass. Report every user/system pair, both medians of user+system seconds and their difference; branch minus main is strictly below 0.3 s, the literal local A/B limit in Performance impact.

The temporary harness implements all startup/runtime measurements in Performance impact and reports raw values. Startup: report utime+stime at first readyz 200 for a format-3 ledger copy and format 4. Runtime: 200 checks (100 HTTP, 50 TLS, 50 domain), 50 components, fresh per-request timestamps, 1000-ms polling, 20-s warm-up and a 60-s measurement for main, branch without alerts and branch with all three alerts. Report /proc CPU, VmRSS and VmHWM for all three; branch-without-alerts minus main is at most 0.1 s CPU and 3 MiB VmHWM, and branch-with-alerts minus main is at most 0.3 s CPU and 3 MiB VmHWM.

With the local fake API and file-channel config of completion check 8, PULSE_NOTIFY_POLL_MS=1000 and alerts budget-low/tls-expiry, report the exact environment/command and output file lines: after 10 polls exactly 1 budget-low and 1 tls-expiry line.

The PR body names issue lorenzh/pulse-meta#571 and records the required checks, main-red/branch-green names and failure lines, allowed expectation changes, security checklist results, all raw performance measurements/limits, manual file lines, Compose SHAs/image/output and CI results. It documents renewal inside 14 days not recognized, next-due-only late subscriptions, dropped incidents of warning-only channels, downgrade via the v3 backup and warnings up to 2 times intervalMs late.
